messages:
deploy-bot: Starting blue->green rollout to eu-west: weight shift 10% -> 40% -> 100% over 30m. image=runtime:v2.3.1. tags: release/2026-03-15
incident-bot: Alert: rate(502) spike in eu-west during rollout. threshold breached (5m). metric: frontend.502.count. see: https://dashboards.redwood/alerts/502-eu-west
anna.sre: I’m on pager, joining. hitting the graphs now. 502s correlate with a subset of green instances only.
michael.eng: looking at logs from green pods — a lot of TLS handshake failures with backend model route: "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority". thats odd, green was built with same cert bundle.
dave.oncall: paging infra to confirm cert distribution to the new ASG/instances. @ops-bot do we have any config drift alerts?
ops-bot: Config drift scan started for eu-west group 'green-pool-03'. Missing file: /etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem on 3/12 instances.
jess.support: Support reports a few customers in EU complaining about generation failures and timeouts. ticket count: 7 in last 10m.
maya.product: quick check — any big customer traffic routed to green? we were supposed to route only non-critical traffic for canary.
michael.eng: the rollout control plane shifted weight too quickly due to mis-evaluated latency metric. green got ~30% of production traffic earlier than intended.
anna.sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip feature-flag kill-switch to halt green traffic; 2) revert DNS/weights back to blue; 3) drain green and re-deploy with cert. Fastest is kill-switch.
dave.oncall: I’ll take lead on kill-switch. handing off pager to @anna.sre after action.
dave.oncall: Executing kill-switch (feature flag) now — calling flag-api: 
```
curl -X POST "https://flags.redwood/api/v1/flags/enable" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FLAG_API_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"flag":"bluegreen_pause_eu_west","value":true}'
```
incident-bot: Flag change detected: bluegreen_pause_eu_west = true by dave.oncall at 1778504458. Traffic routing paused to green in eu-west.
michael.eng: seeing immediate drop in 502s on graphs. using tail -f on logstream to confirm.
anna.sre: good. start validating green instances are drained and that restart isn't causing collateral. can we confirm which instances missed certs? ops-bot?
ops-bot: Drift report: instances i-0a12b, i-0b34c, i-0c56d missing /etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem. All in green-pool-03.
michael.eng: we should rotate certs or bootstrap CA bundle then redeploy green, but keep green paused for now.
jess.support: Customer-facing note: drafting message for affected EU customers. ETA 10m. @maya.product can you review for tone?
maya.product: will review. emphasize temporary and that we're pausing rollout; include ETA for full restore.
anna.sre: Incident severity initial: Sev2 (partial outage for subset of EU requests). Impact: approx 3% of EU users saw 502s during the 10–15m window before kill-switch.
dave.oncall: rolling back routing for safety confirmed: flag pause worked; reverting any unintended traffic shifts.
michael.eng: capture for postmortem: root cause appears to be config drift on a minority of green instances + rollout automation moving weights too aggressively because latency threshold trigged incorrectly. Also need a stronger pre-flight cert check in pipeline.
anna.sre: next steps: 1) keep blue traffic at 100% until green re-bootstrap; 2) ops to remediate missing certs on green nodes; 3) eng to add pre-deploy cert validation & fail-rollout if mismatch; 4) change rollout automation to require time-based step confirmation not only metric.
ops-bot: Remediation ticket created: INT-2026 eu-west-green-cert-fix. Assigned: ops-team. Playbook link: https://playbooks.redwood/incidents/eu-green-cert-fix
dave.oncall: Handoff: I’ll remain until ops confirms remediation, then @anna.sre will own post-incident follow-ups and PM.
anna.sre: Accepted handoff. I’ll coordinate postmortem and customer impact summary. Please drop any relevant logs/links here.
michael.eng: saving logs and a filtered dump: 
```
# sample: TLS errors from green pod
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z green-pod-7f9e TLS error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-03-15T14:13:12Z green-pod-8a1c TLS error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```
jess.support: Sent initial customer message to impacted accounts (7 tickets). Link to inbox: https://support.redwood/tickets?q=eu+502
maya.product: Customer comm: "We've temporarily paused the new rollout in EU while we investigate a certificate distribution issue affecting a small portion of traffic. No action needed from customers. We'll update when services are fully restored."
anna.sre: Timeline notes for postmortem: 
- 1778504321: rollout initiated to eu-west (deploy-bot)
- 1778504390: alert: 502 spike (incident-bot)
- 1778504458: kill-switch enabled (dave.oncall) -> green traffic paused
- 1778504520: 502s decreased to baseline
- 1778504800: ops remediation started
- 1778505600: ops reports first pass remediation complete on green instances (certs installed), green remains paused pending redeploy

anna.sre: Severity final for incident record: Sev2. Impact summary: ~3% EU requests, ~12 minutes visible consumer impact window, no data loss.
michael.eng: action items: ENG-3142 add preflight cert check, ENG-3143 rollout automation safe-guard (enforce step wait + manual approve at >20% traffic), ENG-3144 add canary cert verification job.
jess.support: will follow up with all affected tickets and mark as updated once green is fully redeployed.
dave.oncall: closing active pager for now. handing final notes to @anna.sre. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident update saved to timeline. link: https://incidents.redwood/1778504321
anna.sre: I’ll set a blameless postmortem and invite ops/eng/release owners. Closing this thread — we’ll reopen if regressions show. Thanks all for quick triage. :heart:
